## Body

PR #239 round two at fe6811f6bc18be5c46690cfdbf4c8b951a9dc83c closes the earlier default-redirect note: the shared client explicitly uses Policy::none and an integration regression asserts a returned 302 plus zero hits on a second listener (crates/cache-proxy/src/proxy.rs:243-260; tests/proxy.rs:499-518). req-14 projects header bytes into closed main/subagent and agent/user logging labels; this does not sanitize unrelated model/path fields. The stale-refresh account/generation check runs under the token write lock before either success or failure processing (proxy.rs:547-594). Bearer assertions show account B survives an account A refresh, but a shared-upstream test does not prove atomic token/endpoint snapshots. The readiness-facts mutant survives even though its production guard remains: serialized checks support eventual replacement, not absence of transient observations by forwarding, which does not take check_lock. Treat that surviving mutant as an honest security proof limit absent an actual credential/destination exploit; do not restate it as unobservable. Final verdict is pass-with-notes in outputs/2026-11/18-verdict-pr-239-fe6811f.dd.json. Exact-head CI artifact 14393906188 contains 20 unit and 10 integration cache-proxy passes. Mutation receipts were inspected, not reproduced.
